_comment: Global balance parameters. The Act 1 simulation (aethelgard.core.simulation) uses these values.

xp._armorComment: Armor XP per hit = monster XP x defenseXpPerHit x min(1, share mitigated / armorXpFullAtMitigation). Low-level armor mitigates ~10%; at 0.25 that already gives ~40% of the full XP per hit, in line with the Act 1 simulation (armor share 15%).

levelFactor._comment: XP factor by Δ = monster level − proficiency level (D2 table below level 25). Outside −10..+10 the edge value applies; missing = 1.0.

attributes._comment: What each attribute point does (GDD 4.2). Strength: physical damage. Dexterity: accuracy, critical chance, defense. Intelligence: spell damage (and Energy, in character). Vitality: life (in character). weaponMasteryPerLevel: a weapon hits harder as its proficiency grows (+4% per level above 1 of Blades for a sword, Archery for a bow, Maces, Two-Handed, Dual Wield with two weapons), the way spells grow with their skill level.

combat._meleeEdge: A melee hit on someone who fights from range (a bow, or a monster that shoots) gets this much more damage and accuracy: closing in on an archer pays off, for players and monsters alike.
combat._rangedKite: Archers and casters step back from anyone closer than rangedKiteTiles before shooting again; cornered (a wall or a body behind them), they shoot from where they are.

dualWield._comment: Two one-hand weapons (GDD 7, D2 style): swings alternate main → off; each hand uses its own weapon. The off hand deals offHandDamageMult of its damage (Off-Hand Training adds to it, never above 1). No guard and no Shield actives without a shield.

bow._comment: Bows (two-handed): the attack fires an arrow at the target's position when it is within the bow's rangeTiles and in sight. arrowSpeed in tiles/s.

townPortal._comment: Always available, no scroll (GDD 10.4): opens where you stand after castSeconds of standing still (moving, attacking or a hard hit stops it), unless you are in town; walking into it takes you to town, and the one in town brings you back and closes it. cooldownSeconds between two portals, counted from when one opens.

loot._comment: Drops fall on the ground around the monster and must be picked up (click, or walk over gold when autoPickupGold). pickupRangeTiles = how close the player must get. Alt shows every label.

death._comment: Death penalty. xpLossPctOfLevel = fraction of the XP already earned INSIDE the current level that is lost (never loses a level). 0 = off in the MVP.

movement._comment: Tiles per second. Diablo 2 runs at 9 yards/s and walks at 6: on screen the hero covers about 3 times its own height per second; with the hero ~94 px tall and a tile ~40 px across, that is ~6.5 tiles/s. Monsters move at monsterBase × their type's moveSpeed (wolf 1.4, zombie 0.6), slower than the player as in Diablo 2.

exits._comment: An exit (edge, entrance, stairs) takes you when you step within touchRadiusTiles of its cell: a target of about three cells instead of one. It fires when you walk in; arriving inside the zone does not send you back until you step out and in again.

guard._comment: Active block (hold the guard button). Blocks physical hits inside the front arc; each block costs Energy. A block never stops everything: it stops blockReduction of the hit (+ shield base + Defensive Stance), at most blockReductionCap, and armor works on what passes. Perfect window at the start of the guard: zero cost, blockReductionCap stopped and counterattack (Parry). After lowering the guard, it can only be raised again after guardRaiseCooldownSeconds (prevents perfect-parry abuse).

collision._comment: Bodies do not overlap: the player and monsters block each other, and monsters block monsters. Radii in tiles; a monster's radius = its type radius x its rank sizeMult. Bodies are about as wide as their sprites (a 0.42 radius is ~19 px each side on screen for a ~45 px wide hero). Walls stop the edge of the body, not only its center: up to wallMarginMax (a corridor one cell wide still fits anyone). A monster type with collides=false (monsters.json) passes through bodies, and the target frame says so.

timing._comment: Action timings (GDD 7.7). All durations in seconds. 'faster…' shortens the duration: duration = base / (1 + bonus).
timing._monsterSwing: A monster's swing (wind-up, hit at half, follow-through) lasts at most monsterSwingSeconds; the rest of its attack interval (1.4 s / attackRate, then x1.3) is a pause between swings, so slow attackers hit as rarely as before but no longer move in slow motion.

magic._comment: Spells (skills.json nodes with 'spell'). A cast lasts castSeconds / (1 + faster cast), and the spell leaves the hand at castReleaseFraction of it. Spells always hit and ignore armor; the target's resistance to the element takes its share (resist cap in combat). Fire walls, burning ground and burning monsters deal their damage every tickSeconds.

monsterAi._comment: Monster behaviours by monsters.json 'ai' (core/monster_ai.py). flanker: wolves come at you from the side (flankOffsetTiles). charger: boars rush in a straight line when you are between chargeMinTiles and chargeMaxTiles, at chargeSpeedMult their speed; touching you deals +chargeDamagePct and stuns for chargeStunSeconds; then chargeCooldown. caster_revive: necromancers raise a dead follower within reviveRadiusTiles at reviveHpPct life every reviveCooldown (raised monsters give no XP or loot). support_heal: shamans heal an ally below healBelowPct life by healPct of its life every healCooldown. sleepTiles: monsters farther than that from every player, and not alert, are not simulated (performance).

party._comment: Co-op (M10-03), Diablo 2 rules by default (core/party.py). With n players in the game, monster life and XP grow by (n+1)/2. A kill's XP gets +35% for each other party member within shareRangeTiles and is split among them in proportion to their character level. loot: shared (D2: drops are for whoever picks them up) or individual (each player gets their own). The chance of a monster dropping nothing is raised to the power (n+1)//2. One player: every rule gives exactly the single-player numbers.
